text:
Kestrelline Rail will build its new maintenance depot in Lowen Ridge, the company announced on 14 March 2025.

Marisol Entwhistle, the company's Chief Operations Officer, confirmed the site selection at a press briefing in the city. The decision is set out in Kestrelline Rail's "Regional Fleet Readiness Plan 2025–2032," the document presented at the briefing and on which this report relies.

The depot is budgeted at 212 million credits. According to the plan, it is expected to employ 640 workers once operational.

The plan frames the facility as a central element of the company's strategy for keeping its regional fleet in service over the next seven years. Lowen Ridge was chosen from among the sites considered, and the company has now formally confirmed the selection.

The announcement settles a question that had been open since the plan's preparation. Kestrelline Rail has not published further detail in the material cited here.
